messages.subject: interaction plots
parts:
Hi All,

Does anyone happen to know of a short way to make interaction plots in
ggplot2?  Something along the order of:

d <- mtcars; xbar <- mean(d$wt); sdx <- sd(d$wt)
m <- lm(mpg ~ hp * wt, d)
d$x <- c(rep(range(d$hp), 3), rep(NA, 26))
d$y <- c(predict(m, data.frame(hp = rep(range(d$hp), 3),
  wt = rep(c(xbar - sdx, xbar, xbar + sdx), each = 2))),
  rep(NA, 26))
d$g <- c(rep(c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD"), each = 2), rep(NA, 26))

require(ggplot2)
ggplot(d, aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = g))

#rm(d, xbar, sdx, m)

but preferably more automated. I am not exactly wild about them, but
Psychology is tremendously fond of using these to break down
interactions so I find myself creating them quite frequently. I know
there are some things like this that use base graphics (e.g., in
TeachingDemos) but I would prefer to stay in the pretty, flexible
environment of ggplot2. If not I will hack something together.

Thanks,

Josh

--
Joshua Wiley
Ph.D. Student, Health Psychology
University of California, Los Angeles

messages.subject: Re: interaction plots
parts:
On Fri, May 20, 2011 at 3:51 AM, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I don't have one either, but if you do hack one together please share or
> feel free to let us help you hack.

Its a crude little thing for a very specific task, but since you asked
here it is:

IntPlot <- function(object, data, x, int, intvals, intnames,
mean = TRUE, n = 100, FUN = "glm", ...) {
require(ggplot2)

if (is.formula(object) && !missing(data)) {
FUN <- match.fun(FUN)
m <- FUN(formula = object, data = data, ...)
## likely not the best way to tell if there is a predict method
} else if (is.data.frame(object$model) &&
is.function(getS3method("predict", class(m)))) {
m <- object
} else stop("'object' must be a formula or an object with an appropriate
method for 'predict' and a copy of the data")

mdata <- m$model
y <- as.character(formula(m)[[2]])

vals <- as.data.frame(lapply(mdata, function(x) {
if (is.numeric(x)) {
if (mean) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else 0
} else {
names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}}))

if (missing(intvals)) {
b <- c(mean(mdata[, int], na.rm = TRUE),
sd(mdata[, int], na.rm = TRUE))
intvals <- rep(c(b[1] - b[2], b[1], b[1] + b[2]), each = n)
intnames <- c("-1 SD", "Mean", "+1 SD")
} else intvals <- rep(intvals, each = n)

newdat <- do.call(rbind, rep(list(vals), length(intvals)))
newdat[, int] <- intvals
minx <- min(mdata[, x], na.rm = TRUE)
maxx <- max(mdata[, x], na.rm = TRUE)
rx <- seq(from = minx, to = maxx, length.out = n)

newdat[, x] <- rep(rx, length(intvals)/n)

preddat <- data.frame(predict(m, newdat, type = "response"),
newdat[, x], factor(rep(intnames, each = n), levels = intnames))
colnames(preddat) <- c(y, x, int)

p <- ggplot(mdata, aes_string(x = x, y = y)) +
geom_point() +
geom_line(aes_string(x = x, y = y, colour = int), data = preddat)
return(p)
}

## Examples of how I will use it (i.e., create a model or using an
existing model object)

m1 <- lm(mpg ~ hp * wt, mtcars)
m2 <- glm(vs ~ hp * wt, family = "binomial", data = mtcars)
IntPlot(cyl ~ hp * wt, mtcars, x = "wt", int = "hp")
IntPlot(cyl ~ hp * wt, mtcars, x = "wt", int = "hp", intvals = c(100,
300), intnames = c("low", "high"))
IntPlot(m1, x = "wt", int = "hp")
IntPlot(m2, x = "wt", int = "hp")

Josh

> Brandon
